1.explanation:
• lib/features/context-pad/ContextPadProvider.js – this is where the context-pad entries are defined. To add the universal “append anything” action you must add a new entry here and wire it to open the popup menu.

• lib/features/context-pad/index.js – this module bootstraps and configures the ContextPadProvider. You need to include and register your new “append menu entries” provider here.

• lib/features/popup-menu/index.js – the popup‐menu feature is responsible for rendering dropdown menus. You must register your new append‐menu‐entries provider alongside the existing ReplaceMenuProvider.

• lib/features/popup-menu/ReplaceMenuProvider.js – this file is the pattern for building a popup menu provider. You will either extend it or duplicate its logic to create an AppendMenuProvider that enumerates all BPMN element types.

• lib/features/modeling/behavior/AppendBehavior.js – the modeling behavior for append actions lives here. You may need to ensure it recognizes the new generic “append anything” command and routes creation through the standard modeling stack.
1.bug_scenario: When you click on an existing element the context-pad (the little toolbar that pops up around a shape) currently only shows specific “append” actions (e.g. append a Task or an Event). The request is to add a single “append anything” entry (a “+” button) to that context pad which opens a dropdown menu listing all possible BPMN elements you can append. In the screenshot you see the existing context-pad with its buttons; the missing button is the one that should open a searchable “Create element” menu of all types.

2.explanation: ContextPadProvider.js is responsible for building the little action pad around selected elements. To show the new append (+) handle and hook it up to a menu, this file needs updating (adding the append entry). The context-pad/index.js file wires all providers into the framework — we must register our new append menu entries provider there. AppendBehavior.js implements the core behavior for appending new elements (creating a shape and connecting it). Ensuring the behavior is wired up correctly and exposed by the context pad is essential for the feature to work.
2.bug_scenario: When selecting an existing BPMN element (e.g. a Task), the context pad that appears only shows a limited set of actions (move, delete, connect, replace), but it does not show the “append” (+) handle that would open a menu listing all possible BPMN elements you can append. The goal is to add an “append anything” entry to the context pad so that clicking the plus icon opens a searchable menu of all element types, just like in the palette.
